hints.content:
###Graphing the first point

To graph a line, we need to find two points that are on it. Then we can drag the movable points to those points.

We already have one point, $(7, 3)$, and we can use the slope of the line to find another point.

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes each scale by one. The point seven, three is plotted and labeled.

hints.content:
###Use the slope to graph another point

We want the slope to be $-\dfrac14$:

$\text{slope}=\dfrac{\purpleD{\text{rise}}}{\maroonD{\text{run}}}=\dfrac{\purpleD{\Delta y}}{\maroonD{\Delta x}}=\dfrac{\purpleD{-1}}{\maroonD{4}}=\dfrac{\purpleD{1}}{\maroonD{-4}}$

Starting at $(7, 3)$, we don't have room on the given grid to go $1$ unit down and $4$ units right. So let's go $\purpleD{1\text{ unit up}}$ and $\maroonD{4\text{ units to the left}}$ to plot another point on the line:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes each scale by one. The points seven, three and three, four are plotted and labeled. There is a vertical dotted segment from seven, three to seven, four that is labeled one. There is a horizontal dotted segment from seven, four to three, four that is labeled negative four.

question.content:
**Graph a line that contains the point $(7, 3)$ and has a slope of $-\dfrac{1}{4}$.**
